Born: February 17, 1963, 1:40 PM local time, Brooklyn, New York, USA. Source: Astro-Databank, Rodden rating AA.

The AA rating means the time comes from a birth certificate or an equally solid record, so the rising sign, the Midheaven and the houses below can be read at face value. Open Michael Jordan's chart on Astrolas to follow along.

One sign carries more weight here than any other: three planets, the Sun, Mercury and Saturn, all sit in Aquarius, a sign the Astrolas library ties to reform, independence and ideas that run ahead of their own time. Nothing in a chart explains a fadeaway jump shot, but a sign this loaded is a fitting signature for a player who changed how his sport looked to the rest of the world.

muc.ten: Sun, Mercury and Saturn together in Aquarius
doan: Three planets share Aquarius: the Sun at 28°23', Mercury at 2°39', and Saturn at 15°32'. Mercury and Saturn both land in the 8th house; the Sun sits one house over, in the 9th.

The library reads the Aquarius Sun as original and future-facing, led by Uranus rather than by convention, someone who measures things by ideas rather than status and often looks ahead of their own era. It names a related challenge too: that same independence can read as distant, eccentric or hard to pin down. Mercury in Aquarius adds a mind drawn to what others haven't noticed yet, logical and only lightly swayed by emotion, with a close read on other people's motives and reactions. Paired with the 8th house, the library reads that as sharp, discreet insight into hidden motives, plus a tendency to hold on to old slights longer than most people would. Saturn in Aquarius brings discipline bent toward reform rather than tradition, strong group leadership, and a placement the library ties to a genuinely difficult youth that, over time, builds into real maturity and self-belief.

Jordan didn't make the varsity team as a sophomore, judged too short at five foot eleven, and spent that season starring for the junior varsity squad instead, a setback he referenced for the rest of his career as fuel. Few athletes have been as openly described, by teammates and opponents alike, as someone who converted being doubted or disrespected into motivation, which lines up neatly with a Mercury in the 8th house that the library says keeps score.

muc.ten: Jupiter conjunct the Midheaven in Pisces
doan: Jupiter sits at 19°06' Pisces, in the 9th house, close enough to the Midheaven (22°28' Pisces) to form a conjunction, orb 3°22'.

The library reads Jupiter in Pisces as compassionate and idealistic, with good fortune that tends to arrive through popularity and an ability to move people emotionally, doing best in fields that serve or inspire others in some way. Jupiter conjunct the Midheaven, which marks the most public point of the chart, the library reads as about as clear a signature of a full, successful life as the chart offers: career success, a stable home, and the respect of a great many people, the result of luck combined with sustained effort rather than luck alone. Its one caution is balance, since that same ambition can crowd out family life if it runs unchecked.

Jordan is usually named first in any conversation about the greatest player basketball has produced, across a career that included six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls and two Olympic gold medals. His fame also reached well past the sport itself, through a namesake shoe line with Nike that turned his image into one of the most recognized in the world, the kind of reach a Jupiter-Midheaven conjunction is built to describe.

muc.ten: Moon in Sagittarius in the 6th house
doan: The Moon sits at 10°01' Sagittarius, in the 6th house of daily work and health.

The library reads the Sagittarius Moon as optimistic and generous, someone who sets big goals and dives in with real enthusiasm, rarely slowed down by the chance of failing, with self-confidence and a kind of luck that often carries the plan through anyway. It loves freedom, new environments and new people, and treats love itself as something closer to an adventure than a settled arrangement. In the 6th house, the library ties that same emotional energy directly to work and routine: colleagues treated like family, emotional health running in step with physical health, and a need to feel useful and engaged every single day rather than just getting by.

That need to feel useful through work, paired with a mind that treats failure as something to shrug off and try again, matches a player whose competitive drive in practice, not only in games, is one of the most repeated stories about him from teammates over the years.

muc.ten: Mars retrograde in Leo in the 2nd house
doan: Mars sits at 9°57' Leo, retrograde, in the 2nd house of money and personal resources.

The library reads Mars in Leo as fire turned up rather than down: a refusal to accept being average, a need to leave a personal signature on whatever is being done, and real talent for performing and leading a team at the same time. Its lesson is pairing that personal brilliance with respect for the group around it rather than overshadowing it. In the 2nd house, with Mars retrograde, the library reads a careful rather than impulsive relationship with earning: real entrepreneurial drive, but one that studies the risk before committing, then pursues the chosen direction with unusual persistence once the decision is made.

Jordan built one of the largest sports-driven business fortunes of his era, not from his playing contracts alone but from ventures he stayed with for decades, including majority ownership of the Charlotte Hornets well after he retired as a player, a pattern that fits a cautious, retrograde Mars more than a reckless one.

muc.ten: Uranus and Pluto, both retrograde, in Virgo in the 3rd house
doan: Uranus sits at 3°28' Virgo and Pluto at 11°12' Virgo, both retrograde, both in the 3rd house of communication and everyday thinking.

Uranus in Virgo and Pluto in Virgo are both generational placements, shared by much of Jordan's birth cohort, but the library still reads each of them through the personal lens of house and motion here. Uranus in Virgo is sharp and analytical, always hunting for a more efficient method and resistant to doing something a certain way just because that's how it has always been done. Retrograde in the 3rd house, that same insight turns inward first: original ideas get tested privately for a long stretch before they are ever spoken aloud. Pluto in Virgo adds a perfectionist, detail-driven need to improve whatever it touches, and the 3rd house reads that as a mind that digs for evidence before drawing any conclusion, speaks rarely, but carries real weight when it finally does.

Jordan's public reputation was built on exactly that pattern: famously short, pointed answers in interviews next to famously long, exacting preparation behind the scenes, ideas worked out alone and in practice long before they ever reached a press conference.

muc.ten: Venus in Capricorn in the 7th house
doan: Venus sits at 13°12' Capricorn, in the 7th house of partnership.

The library reads Venus in Capricorn as cautious and reserved in love rather than quick to open up, often read by others as cooler than it actually is, a kind of protective shell kept up until the relationship has proven it can last. Once that trust is built, the library says, this Venus works hard and sincerely to keep a partner secure, less interested in grand romantic gestures than in steady, demonstrated commitment. In the 7th house, that same instinct extends outward into any close partnership: the library ties it to charm that reads as polished rather than showy, and real benefit, financial or otherwise, that tends to come through a spouse or a close associate.
Its caution, in the library's reading, is confusing a passing infatuation with the real thing, and trusting the wrong person before a relationship has earned it.

muc.ten: What the chart adds up to
doan: Three planets in Aquarius pushing toward reform and reputation, a Jupiter sitting right on the career point, and a 3rd house carrying two retrograde outer planets that keep most of the real thinking private: together they describe someone built to perform in public while doing the real work somewhere nobody is watching. The Sagittarius Moon supplies the refusal to be discouraged, and a retrograde Mars supplies the patience to build wealth and reputation slowly rather than all at once.
